doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Advice to graduating students
summary: Do something else if you can, play for fun, and get out and meet people.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Do you have words of advice for them as they graduate and try to make their way in the business?

Well I tell them if you could do something else it’s probably a good idea to do it, and then play for fun. Because I — the business as such is nothing like it was when I started out. I can’t really advise them too much about what’s happening today. Though I do know the process of getting involved in music and becoming a player and a known player is still the same. It’s social, it’s what drive you have for whatever reason you know.

Probably not money or fame but that you just love the music as I did, and you find a way to do it. But most all my students, if they’re not full time musicians they’re doing something, they’re teaching, they start their own labels, they, you know there’s so many different things that they can do. So they just paid a lot of money to go to college for four years and they end up with a degree in jazz performance and I say, “What are you going to do with that? You can go down to Small’s and show them your document? “Can I sit in you know here’s my B.F.A.” And they think it’s funny but I’m sort of not kidding.
Right. Probably mom and dad are asking the same question.
You’ve got to go play. You’ve got to meet people.
